summary:
VØRAX: The Last Signal is a first-person 3D psychological horror game that turns the legacy of abandoned NASA equipment into an interactive story. After an accident, the player awakens alone aboard an evacuated spacecraft. To restore its systems and secure rescue, they explore dark corridors, recover fragmented archives, and investigate real missions such as Opportunity and InSight. Each recovered artifact activates a radio transmission and an interactive archive sequence that explains the mission’s purpose, discoveries, and lasting scientific impact.

The game addresses NASA Space Apps’ “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge by connecting the protagonist’s isolation with the story of robotic explorers whose operations ended but whose contributions remain. Designed primarily for teens and young adults, VØRAX combines suspense, exploration, and science-based storytelling to make space history more accessible, memorable, and emotionally engaging. Its central message is simple: a mission can stop sending signals without ceasing to matter.
details:
1. What is VØRAX and how does it work?

VØRAX: The Last Signal is a first-person 3D psychological horror game that combines immersive storytelling, scientific exploration, and interactive learning to preserve the legacy of abandoned NASA equipment on the Moon and Mars.

The story begins when the protagonist awakens alone aboard an evacuated spacecraft following an accident. Surrounded by darkness, damaged systems, and mysterious transmissions, the player must investigate the vessel, uncover its secrets, and find a way to survive and secure rescue.

Throughout the experience, players encounter scientific archives and references to real NASA missions. These discoveries connect the player's isolation with the stories of robotic explorers that were left behind after completing their missions.

The gameplay combines first-person exploration, environmental storytelling, scientific questions, and archive-based interactions. Radio transmissions introduce the history, scientific purpose, and discoveries of NASA equipment, transforming historical information into part of the player's journey.

2. How does it address the challenge?

The challenge asks participants to preserve the stories of scientific equipment abandoned on the Moon and Mars.

Rather than creating a conventional educational website or documentary, we use psychological horror as a storytelling mechanism.

Our central narrative establishes a parallel between a human protagonist who has been abandoned and the robotic explorers whose signals have fallen silent.

By discovering their records, the player learns that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its scientific contribution.

Missions such as Opportunity and InSight provide opportunities to explore the discoveries, challenges, and lasting legacy of robotic planetary exploration.

3. Creativity and innovation

VØRAX approaches space education through an unconventional genre: psychological horror.

Instead of presenting scientific information as isolated facts, we integrate it into a narrative built around mystery, suspense, isolation, and discovery.

The game's atmosphere encourages curiosity, while its interactive components invite players to investigate scientific information rather than simply read it.

This creates an emotional connection between players and robotic explorers, transforming machines that might otherwise be forgotten into characters with meaningful stories.

4. Tools and technologies

VØRAX was developed as a browser-based 3D experience using several technologies:

  • TypeScript: Application logic and interactive game systems.
  • Babylon.js: Real-time 3D rendering, scene management, and first-person exploration.
  • Vite: Frontend development and application building.
  • Blender: Exploration of 3D modeling and asset-development workflows.
  • Claude and Codex: AI-assisted programming, debugging, and development support.

Our development approach prioritizes accessibility through web technologies, allowing users to experience the project without installing a conventional desktop game.

5. Intended impact and benefits

Our primary audience consists of teenagers and young adults, particularly those between 15 and 28 years old.

We aim to make planetary exploration more engaging for people who may not normally seek out technical reports, scientific archives, or educational documentaries.

Through interactive storytelling, VØRAX seeks to encourage curiosity about space science, introduce players to the contributions of robotic missions, and communicate the importance of preserving scientific knowledge.

The experience also demonstrates how entertainment technologies can be adapted for informal science education.

6. Design considerations and limitations

During development, we considered several important factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: Historical mission information must be distinguished from fictional narrative elements.
  • Accessibility: Browser-based delivery reduces installation barriers.
  • Engagement: Exploration and suspense encourage players to remain involved with the educational content.
  • Performance: The experience must balance visual atmosphere with real-time rendering requirements.
  • Development constraints: We prioritized a demonstrable prototype and a coherent narrative experience within the limited hackathon timeframe.

Our prototype is an initial demonstration of this concept rather than a complete commercial game. Further development could expand the number of NASA missions represented, strengthen the interactive scientific simulations, and evaluate educational outcomes through user testing.

Conclusion

VØRAX is built around one central idea: being abandoned does not mean being forgotten.

Long after a spacecraft or rover stops functioning, its discoveries can continue influencing humanity's understanding of the universe.

By combining science, storytelling, and interactive entertainment, we aim to give these forgotten explorers a new voice.
